progress.text: · Greek text hyphenates. The patterns were never compiled in, so Greek set unhyphenated however narrow the column; "Greek", "Greek: Greece", el and el-GR all resolve now and ανθρωπος breaks αν-θρω-πος. They are the monotonic patterns (hyph-el-monoton, Dimitrios Filippou, under MIT), which is what polytonic text hyphenates by too. Five of InDesign's ~40 hyphenation languages. No readiness percentage change.

· IDML: ruler guides import and export (they were dropped). Each page's guides come in measured from the document's ruler origin (spread, page or spine), with Fit to Page, Locked and their layer, parent pages' included, and go out again under their pages. No readiness percentage change.

· Find Font no longer reports a style missing when it differs from the installed one only in spacing or case (InDesign files can name Regular  with a trailing space); the text was already drawn in the right face. No readiness percentage change.

· A line of text is set when its baseline fits in the frame, as in InDesign: descenders may hang below the frame's bottom. A frame sized to the cap height of a big heading (103 pt in a 2.77 cm frame, as Zero2Graphic's magazine tutorial draws them) no longer oversets. No readiness percentage change.

· A story that ends with a return is no longer overset when only its empty last paragraph doesn't fit, as in InDesign (Preflight said "Overset text: 0 characters" for a caption InDesign shows with no errors). No readiness percentage change.

· Flex Layout (InDesign 2026): Object › Flex Layout (Add to, Convert to, Remove) and a Flex Layout panel laid out as InDesign's, also in Properties. A container lays out its objects by direction, wrap, justification, the alignment grid, Fixed/Auto width and height, padding and spacing, after every edit; Add detects aligned objects (direction, Auto size, Space Between at their spacing); resizing a container reflows its objects instead of scaling them; dragging an object in one reorders it. Montilla Design's tutorial replays step for step. No readiness percentage change.

· IDML: the CJK leading model InDesign writes on [No paragraph style] of every document (Aki Below) only applies when the document uses a Japanese composer, as in InDesign; a Western document's paragraphs after a size change no longer sit lower than in InDesign (Montilla Design's Flex Layout file: its captions came out overset). No readiness percentage change.
· The Type tool draws a new text frame over a locked empty frame, as InDesign does, instead of turning the locked frame into a text frame. No readiness percentage change.

· 100% black shows as pure black on screen by default, as InDesign's Appearance of Black does out of the box (Display All Blacks as Rich Black); Preferences › Appearance of Black › Display All Blacks Accurately still shows it as the dark grey it prints, and a saved choice is kept. No readiness percentage change.

· Pathfinder keeps the frontmost object, as InDesign does: a photo placed over shapes and intersected with them shows through the shapes (it was dropped, and the shapes kept their black fill); Add, Exclude Overlap and Minus Back take the front object's fill too, Subtract still keeps the back one. No readiness percentage change.

· The Color panel's Tint field keeps what is typed while it has focus and applies it on Enter or when it loses focus, clamped to 0–100 %. Typing 60 over 100 % no longer snaps back to 100 after the first digit (10060), and a typed tint is no longer ignored. No readiness percentage change.

· Layout › Margins and Columns and Layout › Create Guides are laid out as InDesign's: Margins in Top/Bottom and Inside/Outside pairs with a link button that makes all four the same, Rows and Columns side by side, Fit Guides to Margins or Page, and a Preview checkbox that shows the change on the canvas before OK. A measurement field works out arithmetic when you leave it (0.4375 in2 becomes 0.875 in). No readiness percentage change.

· The Pathfinder panel is laid out as InDesign's: Paths (Join, Open, Close, Reverse), Pathfinder, Convert Shape and Convert Point, each a row of icon buttons. Join Path closes an open path or joins two at their nearest ends (path.join), and Convert Point makes the selected points plain, corner, smooth or symmetrical (path.convertPoints). No readiness percentage change.

· Type › Fill with Placeholder Text fills a frame with paragraphs of a few sentences, as InDesign does, so one paragraph can be styled on its own (it was one long paragraph, and the filler ran sentences together, "interit.Ovid"). No readiness percentage change.

· The Swatches panel has InDesign's header: a Fill/Stroke proxy, Formatting Affects Container/Text and the Tint of the colour in front (a tint alone keeps each object's own swatch). Clicking a swatch applies it to the fill or stroke in front (of the text, when formatting affects text), and the bottom row has New Color Group, New Swatch and Delete Swatch. No readiness percentage change.

· With the Page tool, the Control panel shows the page as InDesign's does: W/H from a reference point, page-size preset (US Business Card added), orientation, Liquid Page Rule (now with Controlled by Parent) and Show Parent Page Overlay, which draws the parent page's size over a resized page. No readiness percentage change.

· On an object-based page the Page tool shows a selected object's liquid pins and resize locks as InDesign does: a click pins a side to the page edge or locks the width or height, with InDesign's tooltips. No readiness percentage change.

· The Liquid Layout panel follows InDesign's: Liquid Page Rule with the page number, Content › Auto-Fit, and Object Constraints › Resize with Page and Pin for the selected object on an object-based page; Create Alternate Layout moved to the Layout menu. No readiness percentage change.

· With the Page tool, the Control panel shows the page as InDesign's does: W/H from a reference point, page-size preset (US Business Card added), orientation, Liquid Page Rule (now with Controlled by Parent) and Show Parent Page Overlay, which draws the parent page's size over a resized page. No readiness percentage change.

· With the Page tool, the Control panel shows the page as InDesign's does: W/H from a reference point, page-size preset (US Business Card added), orientation, Liquid Page Rule and Show Parent Page Overlay, which draws the parent page's size over a resized page. No readiness percentage change.

· The Page tool works as InDesign's: a click selects a page and shows its handles and liquid page rule; dragging a handle previews the rule and springs back, Alt-drag resizes the page from the opposite edge, Shift keeps proportions, with a W/H readout. No readiness percentage change.
· With the Page tool, a guide dragged from a ruler is a liquid guide (dashed), as in InDesign; guide-based pages stretch the objects it crosses. No readiness percentage change.

· The Pages panel menu follows InDesign's order: Insert Pages…, Move Pages…, Duplicate Spread (and at End of Document), Delete Page/Spread, New Parent…, Apply Parent to Pages, Override All Parent Page Items, Parent Pages, Create Alternate Layout…, Numbering & Section Options…, Allow Selected Spread to Shuffle. No readiness percentage change.

· Pages panel: Alt-drag copies a page, a page dropped on Create new page is duplicated at the end, Edit page size offers the presets and Custom Page Size…; duplicated pages keep their own size, rule and guides; thumbnails of pages of their own size stay in their rows. No readiness percentage change.

· In a facing document, pages take their side from their section's page numbers, as InDesign shuffles them: a section that starts at 1 on a left page moves it to the right and the pages after it follow, with their objects. No readiness percentage change.

· The Type menu follows InDesign's order (Size, Character ⌘T, Paragraph ⌥⌘T, Glyphs, the style panels, Notes, footnotes and endnotes, then the insert submenus and Show Hidden Characters); Current Page Number has ⌥⇧⌘N. No readiness percentage change.
· Colour parameters: a bare {c,m,y,k} is always read as 0..100, so C 1 is a 1 % tint and no longer

· The Tools panel follows InDesign's: Gradient Swatch and Gradient Feather are tools of their own; in two columns Content Collector and Placer, Apply Color / Gradient / None and Normal / Preview each get a button; View Options holds Frame Edges, Rulers, Guides, Smart Guides, Baseline Grid and Hidden Characters; Apply Color (,) and Apply Gradient (.) reuse the last colour and gradient. No readiness percentage change.
· Georgian interface (ka, Edit ▸ Interface Language ▸ ქართული): every catalog key

· Switching between document and parent pages refreshes the canvas immediately, preventing black parent pages and stale document objects when the zoom stays the same. Ordinary edits retain partial repainting. No readiness percentage change.

· Object › Fitting has InDesign's shortcuts: Fill Frame Proportionally ⌘⌥⇧C, Fit Content Proportionally ⌘⌥⇧E, Fit Frame to Content ⌘⌥C, Fit Content to Frame ⌘⌥E, Center Content ⌘⇧E. No readiness percentage change.

· Gradients between process colours blend as inks, as InDesign shows them: magenta to cyan passes through C 50 M 50 (a light lilac) on screen instead of the darker RGB mix, and a midpoint between CMYK or grey stops no longer turns the PDF shading RGB. No readiness percentage change.

· Copy with a placed graphic selected (Direct Selection) copies just the graphic, uncropped, where it sits on the page and without the frame's stroke, so Paste Into puts the whole image in place; Cut and Delete then remove only the graphic and leave its frame empty. Nested selections copy in their spread coordinates. No readiness percentage change.

· Object effects (Basic Feather, Inner Glow, shadows, glows, bevel, satin, directional and gradient feathers) apply to frames with pasted-in content, on screen and in image exports: the frame, its clipped content and its stroke are one object to the effect. PDF export still has no soft effects for any object. No readiness percentage change.
· Links rows show their source paths; selecting a link shows its full path wrapped inside the panel, so same-named files from different folders can be distinguished. No readiness percentage change.

· The Text Wrap panel is laid out as InDesign's: the wrap buttons with Invert, and the four offsets (Top, Left, Bottom, Right) showing the object's values, with the link button that sets them all the same. It used to show a single offset, always 0. No readiness percentage change.

· Radial gradients stretch with the object's box, as InDesign draws them: by default an ellipse reaching the frame's sides (it was a circle reaching only the longer side), and a Gradient Swatch tool drag keeps the box's proportions; on screen and in PDF. No readiness percentage change.

· The Window menu follows InDesign's order (Arrange, Workspace, then the panels alphabetically with Color, Editorial, Object & Layout, Styles… submenus), and Window › Workspace lists the workspaces as InDesign does, now with Essentials Classic: the Control panel and an icon column of named panel groups. No readiness percentage change.

· Create Outlines makes one compound path per line (and per text colour within a line), grouped, as InDesign does: Ungroup then leaves each line on its own to be spaced and made into one compound path again. A single line in one colour stays a single compound path. No readiness percentage change.

· Gradient swatches work on strokes: drawn across the path's box on screen and in PDF (they drew nothing), set with object.gradient {target: stroke} and in the Gradient panel when the Stroke box is in front; the stroke's gradient vector moves with the shape and round-trips through IDML. No readiness percentage change.
